newsitem.title: UK: London gold eases under pressure before Easter.
newsitem.headline: London gold eases under pressure before Easter.

text.p: Precious metals prices edged lower on Thursday afternoon in thin trading ahead of the Easter holiday weekend, dealers said.
Bullion was fixed at $348.15 an ounce, compared to $349.50 in the morning and $346.05 on Wednesday afternoon.
Dealers attributed the downward drift to a bit of fund selling originating in New York's Comex futures market.
"Half of the market is on holiday, but that means a little activity can make an impact," a dealer said.
European markets will be closed on Friday and Monday for the Easter holiday. U.S. markets reopen on Monday.
In New York, June gold was down $2.10 at $351.40 shortly after the afternoon gold fixing, erasing most of the gains from a sharp short-covering rally late on Wednesday.
The rally had been boosted by news that the size of the massive Busang gold deposit in Indonesia may have been overstated.
"Gold certainly rallied about $1 on that news, which was a valid move in a short market," a dealer said. "But fundamentally it doesn't change the fact that gold is still in a downtrend."
But some dealers said the Busang news would continue to keep the market on edge until more more details were reported.
Silver followed gold's lead to also edge a couple of cents lower, to $5.12/$5.14 an ounce.
A halfhearted probe of the $5.08/$5.10 support area in the afternoon found no follow-through selling and dealers said silver was well defended on the downside.
But none of the precious metals markets showed signs of moving out of well-worn price ranges.
Platinum was $1.00 weaker at $371.50/$372.50, after trading in a $4.00 price range.
Palladium was barely changed at $145.50/$146.50 an ounce, up $0.50.
The market was in a holding pattern pending fresh news on delayed supply talks between major producer Russia and importer Japan, dealers said.
